ESTABLISHING STILL of Gaya harbour huts, intro-card painted world, same film stock: watercolor-and-oil, 2.5D timber posts, manga ink on thatch, NOT photoreal. WIDE. ONE DEVICE: three stilt granaries on still water from the attached board — KEEP thatch roofs, timber posts, stairs, waterline. IGNORE the modern railing, streetlamp, white box. Mist, pale paper sky, one hard key raking the posts. Empty of people. No text. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. Sensual and suggestive by shape and motion alone, never anatomical, never explicit. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
